summary: Perry County steel fire tower, about 110 ft (33.5 m) tall, in a 1943 survey note; the Forest Lookouts site lists it as removed.

facts.design: steel four-legged structure with an enclosed cabin at the top
facts.status_note: Listed as removed on the Forest Lookouts site; no removal date is given.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey recovery note of 1943 describes the steel fire tower, about 110 feet high

evidence.supports: 1943 recovery note by Coast and Geodetic Survey
evidence.quote: RECOVERY NOTE BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1943 (KBJ)

evidence.supports: standard lookout of the U.S. Forestry Service; steel, four-legged, enclosed cabin, about 110 feet
evidence.quote: THE FIRE TOWER IS A STANDARD LOOKOUT OF THE U.S. FORESTRY SERVICE. IT IS A STEEL, FOUR-LEGGED STRUCTURE WITH AN ENCLOSED CABIN AT THE TOP ABOUT 110 FEET IN HEIGHT.

evidence.supports: survey station sat on a prominent hill
evidence.quote: THIS TRAVERSE STATION IS LOCATED ON A PROMINENT HILL ABOUT 2.5 MILES

evidence.supports: traverse from survey station to tower center, 22.619 m (74.21 feet)
evidence.quote: A TRAVERSE CONNECTION WAS MADE FROM TRIANGULATION STATION TO THE CENTER OF THE LOOKOUT TOWER, DISTANCE 22.619 METERS (74.21 FEET).

evidence.supports: survey sighted on the center of the tower top
evidence.quote: THE POINT OBSERVED UPON WAS THE CENTER OF THE FIRE TOWER AT THE TOP.

notes_for_editor: Single source: the Forest Lookouts page, which reproduces NGS data sheet text (PID BV1504) with a 1943 recovery note and a Removed label. The record's agency was empty; the agency here is the name used in the 1943 note, which may not match a later operator. Three searches found no build date, staffing, fire, or removal date for a Beaumont tower; most hits concerned Beaumont, Texas. Site today unknown; no access data added. Record height_m 33.5 matches the 110 ft in the note.
